title.narrative: Strengthened Ebola Communications in Senegal and Guinea-Bissau

description.narrative: CAFOD is in a ‘Be Safe’ partnership project with CRS and Caritas International. CAFOD will support CRS and CI through funding over the course of 12 months. Be Safe's overarching goal is that Senegal and Guinea-Bissau have increased capacity to prevent disease outbreaks and to enable them to respond more effectively and efficiently to any future emergencies in compliance with international humanitarian principles and standards. A full 12 months is necessary to enable messages to evolve and to allow time for the multiple steps leading to behaviour adoption and sustainability of desired behaviour. Through Prochaska's Stages of Change trans theoretical model of behaviour change, people move through the stages of pre-awareness, awareness/contemplation, actual change/action, practice/maintenance of behaviours, etc. and this process takes multiple reinforcements and methods of messaging. For the project's success it is imperative that the intervention accompany individuals through this process all the way through behaviour adoption and maintenance of the behaviour over time and help recover if there is a relapse of behaviour. The strategic objective is that communities in Senegal and Guinea-Bissau limit transmission of Ebola. Success will be measured through the attainment of three core outputs: Output 1: Technically and culturally appropriate messages on disease prevention and control are developed Output 2: Community leaders have increased capacity to deliver accurate information about Ebola Output 3: Community members have increased knowledge of Ebola and how to protect themselves As CRS' approach places communities at the core of its response, the messages and information sharing systems that Be Safe will put into place will enhance community ownership of, participation in, and control over the project and its outcomes, ensuring adoption and long term sustainability of project-promoted key prevention/protection behaviours.
